title: Make Papyrus MCP onboarding repeatable on a stable HTTPS URL
description:
## Intent

Avoid plugin recreation across fixture/service restarts. Keep the first real ChatGPT pilot on the already-supported configured public client, then add zero-secret client metadata for compatible hosts as a separate, explicitly ordered change.

## Steps

1. For PPY-17c201, use one approved persistent test origin and exact /api/mcp resource for the entire trial. Reserve host, issuer, callback allowlist and client ID before creating any connection. Use the currently supported preregistered public client, S256 and token endpoint method none. Do not rely on a rotating tunnel hostname or change the installed endpoint after a process restart. Choose an already approved HTTPS test environment or request the specific shared-infrastructure approval if none exists.
2. After the first host verification, add Client ID Metadata Document resolution as an opt-in alternative in lib/mcp/oauth-clients.ts and OAuth discovery. Accept operator-pinned exact HTTPS metadata document URLs for approved hosts, never arbitrary client-supplied fetch destinations. Validate status, bounded JSON, exact self-identifying client_id, registered redirect URIs and public token authentication method. Disable fetch redirects. Restrict egress to pinned destinations and refuse private/loopback resolution. Verify the connected address against the validated DNS result to prevent rebinding. Bound cache to at most one hour and fail closed on expiry if refresh fails. Preserve explicit preregistration as fallback. Do not add an open dynamic registration endpoint to Papyrus in this initiative.
3. Keep consent mandatory and the server site/Account-bound. Support only exact configured HTTPS callback URIs and existing reviewed loopback callbacks. Include issuer, resource and host state in tests. A successful metadata lookup grants no tool access by itself. Record the registration mode per host and keep runtime gates independent of the mode. Share DataParade's valid metadata, identifier mismatch, unsafe target, redirect mismatch and expired-cache test cases. Add WWW-Authenticate scope guidance only for an actually granted and enforced scope.

## Gherkin acceptance

Feature: Reuse one Papyrus MCP installation
Scenario: The HTTPS server restarts
  Given a host has installed the site using its stable HTTPS address
  When the server restarts and the user reconnects from that installation
  Then metadata and OAuth still identify the same issuer and resource
  And no new installation or secret is required

Scenario: A client supplies a metadata URL outside the reviewed list
  Given a publication accepts client metadata for approved hosts
  When an authorization request names an unknown or redirected document
  Then the service refuses it without fetching an unapproved destination
  And the request creates no grant

## Verification

Start with the stable URL rehearsal on preregistration. Then add fixture coverage for the supported metadata method and record each tested host. A host limited to an unsupported registration mode is a compatibility finding.
